devices.name: Metonymy
devices.definition: Naming something by a word closely associated with it — cause for effect, container for contents, author for writings.

occurrences.note: " I... have poured out my soul before the Lord ": i.e., my desires and longings
"And the Lord hath given me my petition (i.e., Samuel) which I asked Him for": i.e., the object of my prayer
Our English " hundreds," as applied to a territorial division, has the same origin. 4. God is put for the sacrifices offered to Him
" Then said Jonathan, My father hath troubled the land ": i.e., the People
"And also the eternity of Israel will not lie nor repent." Here, the A.V. renders it " Strength," but the attribute " Eternity" is put for Him to whom it is attributed: i.e., the eternal One: i.e.,…
" And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he": i.e., its inhabitants
Eating and drinking is put for living or being alive

devices.name: Ellipsis
devices.definition: A word or words deliberately left out, to be supplied by the reader — compression and force.

occurrences.note: " Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth."
" And he tarried seven days, according to the time that Samuel [had appointed]."

devices.name: Idiom
devices.definition: A peculiar usage of the Hebrew or Greek that does not carry its literal force — an idiom to be rendered by its sense, not word for word.

occurrences.note: where the figure is rendered " God save," " God save the king." The Heb. is " Let the king live." So also

" his heart died within him "). The word " life " has also the same usage

devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

occurrences.note: "That he (Samuel) may appear before the Lord, and there abide for ever ": i.e., as long as he lives
" And Saul numbered the people that were found (i.e., were present) with him, about six hundred men."
" Nevertheless Saul spake not anything that day ": i.e., concerning David or about his absence. He did speak, f)f course, but not specifically about the matter referred to

devices.name: Heterosis
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — of tense, number, person, degree, or mood (e.g. a future used for a command).

occurrences.note: " Lo,' the days are coming, and I have cut off thine arm": i.e., shall cut off
"Thou hast found ": i.e., wilt find

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

occurrences.note: Truly " the Lord seeth not as man seeth." How many hirelings are there who are engaged in merely washing sows and amusing goats, instead of seeking out and feeding Christ's harassed and scattered a
"As saith the proverb of the ancients, ' Wickedness proceedeth from the wicked: but mine hand shall not be upon thee.' "

devices.name: Rhetorical question
devices.definition: A question asked for effect, not for an answer — to affirm, deny, or provoke thought.

devices.name: Anthropopatheia
devices.definition: Ascribing to God human feelings, parts, or actions, by way of condescension to us.

occurrences.note: " A man after his own heart": i.e., His own Divine and eternal purpose; having regard, not to David's worthiness or unworthiness, but to God's own will

devices.name: Catachresis
devices.definition: One word used for another only remotely related — a deliberately incongruous transfer.

devices.name: Epizeuxis
devices.definition: Immediate repetition of a word for intense emphasis, with nothing between (“Lord, Lord”).

devices.name: Hyperbole
devices.definition: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally, that drives a point home vividly.

devices.name: Paronomasia (wordplay)
devices.definition: A play on words that sound alike but differ in sense — pun, rhyme, near-repetition.

devices.name: Antimetabole
devices.definition: Words repeated in reverse order and grammatical relation (“sabbath for man … man for sabbath”).

devices.name: Hendiadys
devices.definition: One idea expressed by two words joined with “and,” the second really qualifying the first.

devices.name: Pleonasm
devices.definition: A deliberate redundancy — more words than strictly needed — to underline or solemnise.

occurrences.note: " And there was honey upon the ground." Lit., upon the face 0/ the ground, i.e., spread out
"The Lord that delivered me out of the paw (hand) of the lion, and out of the paw (hand) of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine": i.e., the power of the lion, and the bea

devices.name: Polysyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions (“and … and …”) piled up to slow the pace and weight every item.

occurrences.note: and the covenants (which precede the Law

devices.name: Ampliatio
devices.definition: An old name kept for a person or thing after the reason for it has passed (“the blind man” once healed).

devices.name: Antonomasia
devices.definition: A proper name replaced by a descriptive title, or a title by a proper name (“the Son of man”).

devices.name: Asyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions omitted between items in a series, producing a rapid, piled-up effect.

occurrences.note: " And Saul said unto the Kenites, —Go, — depart, — get you down from among the Amalekites, — lest I destroy you with them."

devices.name: Epanadiplosis
devices.definition: A clause encircled — beginning and ending with the same word.

devices.name: Euphemism
devices.definition: A softened or decent expression put for one that is harsh or delicate (“fallen asleep”).

devices.name: Gnome (quotation)
devices.definition: A quotation or proverbial maxim woven in — a pithy saying cited for authority or point.

occurrences.note: a I " To obey b I Is better than sacrifice, a I And to hearken b I Than the fat of rams." Here, again, we have obedience and sacrifice set in contrast. And that is exactly what we have in

devices.name: Hysteresis
devices.definition: A later passage supplying a detail not recorded in the earlier narrative it refers to.

devices.name: Irony
devices.definition: Saying the opposite of what is meant, so the real sense is felt through the contrast.

devices.name: Maledictio
devices.definition: An imprecation or pronouncement of woe (“Woe to you…”).

devices.name: Parable
devices.definition: A continued simile — a narrative laid alongside a truth to teach it by comparison.

occurrences.note: We read of " the proverb," " Is Saul also among the prophets?"

devices.name: Parallelism
devices.definition: Successive lines echo one another in structure — saying the same thing twice, or balancing matched clauses.

occurrences.note: a I " The name of the one was Hannah, b I and the name of the other was Peninnah: b I And Peninnah had children, a I but Hannah had no children."

devices.name: Personification
devices.definition: Giving human traits, action, or speech to something impersonal or abstract.

occurrences.note: They thus confess Him as beyond

devices.name: Polyptoton
devices.definition: Repetition of the same root word in different inflections (“dying you shall die”).

occurrences.note: "All Israel shouted with a great shout": i.e., with a very loud and prolonged or sustained cry

devices.name: Syllogismus
devices.definition: The conclusion is left unstated, so the hearer is made to draw it — an unspoken inference.

devices.name: Synonymia
devices.definition: Amassing synonyms — words of like meaning — to enforce and enlarge a point.
